### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind (double-anonymised): all submissions, first or revised, must be anonymised; names and affiliations go only on a detachable cover sheet; authors replace their own name with "author" in the text and must not list their own publications under "Author" in the references (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions ; "double-anonymized peer review across all papers", why-publish copy 2024-11-19). Forum pieces are reviewed by the Forum Editor and may go to external review (instructions copy) |

| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. The pages read say nothing about publishing reports |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev, n = 5: an average of 2.0 review rounds and 2.3 review reports per manuscript (https://scirev.org/journal/applied-linguistics/, retrieved 2026-11-23). No journal statement |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No reviewer-guidance page was found on the pages read |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the journal's instructions for authors, Wayback copy dated 2024-04-06 (https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) unless another page is named. Rules may have changed since; the live page returns 403 to curl.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research articles reporting empirical research that foregrounds real-world relevance; Forum pieces (commentary, statements on current issues, short research reports, replies); book reviews by invitation only (unsolicited reviews not accepted); special thematic issues, one a year (instructions copy). The home page copy of 2026-11-17 adds a permanent section "AI in Applied Linguistics" |
| **Word limit** | Accepted manuscripts "should not exceed 8,500 words including all material for publication in the print version of the article, except for the abstract"; discourse data in text boxes counts; additional material can go online (instructions copy). A 2022 secondary review summary says 8,500 words inclusive of references (https://journalreviews.princeton.edu/2022/09/17/applied-linguistics); the instructions do not name references separately. Forum pieces normally no longer than 2,000 words; book reviews normally no longer than 1,500 words |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The instructions word the limit as a maximum for accepted manuscripts; no statement on exceptions found |
| **Abstract limit** | No longer than 175 words (instructions copy); keywords: no rule in the copy read. A biodata of about 90 words per contributor goes on the title page |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found. Oxford HumSoc style, author-date citations in the text, endnotes rather than footnotes, no more than two heading levels below the title, headings not numbered (instructions copy) |
| **Supplementary material** | Only directly relevant material in the full text; other supporting material may be published online-only as Supplementary Data, submitted for review in separate files, and cannot be altered after acceptance (instructions copy) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures and tables are marked in the text and supplied at the end or in a separate file, numbered with captions; alt text for figures is requested with the captions (instructions copy) |
| **Style / submission format** | Online submission only; English; British or American spelling allowed, stated by the author and consistent; single quotation marks; serial comma; -ize endings; line numbers included; no page breaks inserted; no electronic style sheet (instructions copy). Data: the journal "strongly encourages" making data and code available where ethically feasible and requires public datasets to be cited in the reference list |

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries were not counted: Crossref records carry no country field and the OpenAlex daily budget ran out before the author-country count could be taken (HTTP 429). The editorial panel is international (per-country counts below) and the publisher's why-submit page claims readers in 106 countries in 2022 (Wayback copy 2024-11-19, https://web.archive.org/web/20241119112301/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/why-publish), a publisher claim not independently checked |
| **Editorial-board geography** | 34 entries recounted from the board page (Wayback copy dated 2026-04-19, https://web.archive.org/web/20260419191530/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/Editorial_Board): USA 14, United Kingdom 7, Brazil 3, Sweden 2, and one each in Colombia, Qatar, Canada, Finland, Germany, Australia and Singapore, plus the editorial-office contact, who has no country printed (14+7+3+2+7+1 = 34; the seven single-entry countries are Colombia, Qatar, Canada, Finland, Germany, Australia, Singapore) |

The home page copy of 2026-11-17 features a virtual issue "Applied Linguistics, Social Problems, and Social Change" covering race and class in English language teaching, gender-inclusive language in Spanish, diversity and equity of knowledge, and representation in the American Association of Applied Linguistics (https://web.archive.org/web/20261117190624/https://academic.oup.com/applij) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, as a scope rule: the journal "welcomes submissions that offer new knowledge about language-related problems and solutions in real-world contexts" and wants papers that foreground "the real-world relevance of research on language with regard to the context, the design, and the implications" (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions; same idea on the about page, copy 2026-04-18).
- **What kind of engagement?** The instructions list four signs of poor fit and ask authors to consider other venues if their paper has: no clear connection with a real-world context; a primary aim of insight into a research methodology or theoretical construct with minimal attention to application; applied implications mentioned only at the end in one or two short paragraphs; no empirical basis (instructions copy). Applied settings named: education, the workplace, healthcare, legal systems and the media (about page copy).
- **Article type and length**: research articles up to 8,500 words, Forum pieces up to 2,000 words (see Format).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: a new permanent section "AI in Applied Linguistics" (editorial https://doi.org/10.1093/applin/amag050); two special issues listed on the home page copy of 2026-11-17: "Considering 'Trans-' Perspectives in Language Theories and Practices" and "Innovation in Research Methods".
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the instructions say authors should consider other venues if the paper fits the listed criteria (instructions copy). SciRev has 2 immediate rejections of 5 reviews, one with the stated reason that the topic was "too specialized" (https://scirev.org/reviews/applied-linguistics/, self-report, n = 1 for that reason).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: regex matches over title plus abstract of Crossref records dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23; 340 of 471 records have an abstract, so counts are lower bounds; shares use 340 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement or a clearly dominant count. Scores measure how often a method appears in abstracts, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows fit this journal better than a formal-linguistics journal; rows that fit only partly say so. Regexes are A1 to A24 in AI-Research Notes.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | Quantitative, statistical, survey or questionnaire wording 84 (24.7%, A1); experiment, intervention or control-group wording 29 (8.5%, A2). The instructions favour empirical research (https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) but name no particular design |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | Interview, focus-group, thematic-analysis, grounded-theory or "qualitative" wording 80 (23.5%, A4) |
| Autoethnography | 1 | 1 of 340 (0.3%, A9). The row fits only marginally; no editorial statement |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "theoretical, conceptual, theorize" 50 (14.7%, A10). The count score is qualified by the journal's own guidance: papers whose main aim is insight into a theoretical construct with minimal attention to application, and papers not based on empirical research, are listed among poor fits (instructions copy) |
| Mixed methods | 2 | 10 of 340 (2.9%, A7) |
| Meta-analysis | 2 | Meta-analysis, systematic review, research synthesis or scoping review 5 (1.5%, A8) |
| Corpus-based analysis (added row) | 3 | "corpus, corpora" 44 (12.9%, A3); 11 record titles carry the word |
| Conversation and discourse analysis (added row) | 3 | Conversation analysis, discourse analysis, multimodal or critical discourse wording 46 (13.5%, A6) |
| Ethnography (added row) | 3 | "ethnograph-" 20 (5.9%, A5) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Sample: across all 340 abstracts in the window, 191 (56.2%) contain I, we, our or my (regex A24); among the 20 most recent abstracts (dated 2026-09-25 to 2026-11-18), 6 do (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23). Examples: https://doi.org/10.1093/applin/amag104 ("we analyzed 6,528 argumentative and narrative essays"), https://doi.org/10.1093/applin/amag064, https://doi.org/10.1093/applin/amag098. The instructions require anonymised submissions with self-references replaced by "author" (instructions copy 2024-04-06) |
| **Expected density** | Maximum 8,500 words for accepted research articles including all print material except the abstract; Forum pieces 2,000; discourse data counts toward the limit; contributors also supply a biodata of about 90 words on the title page (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract no longer than 175 words; no keyword rule in the copy read (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Writing style notes** | Instructions copy 2024-04-06: Oxford HumSoc reference style; author-date citations; single quotation marks; serial comma; -ize endings; British or American spelling stated and consistent; endnotes not footnotes; headings unnumbered and at most two levels below the title; figures with alt text; no line space between paragraphs and first lines indented; spelling: authors state British or American English and use -ize endings where allowed (https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author-list counts for the records that have one (441 of 471; 30 have none): 1 author 164, 2 authors 135, 3 authors 78, 4 or more 64; the records include non-research items (retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The instructions copy of 2024-04-06 says only that if primary data are included, research participants should have signed a consent form; no ethics-committee approval statement is required in that copy (https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions). The live rules could not be read |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records are about 37% of those with an author list: 164 of 441 (Crossref, includes non-research items; retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Names and institutional affiliations go on a detachable cover sheet; no independent-scholar rule found (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Where ethically feasible, the journal "strongly encourages" making data and code available and requires publicly available datasets to be cited with an identifier such as a DOI, following the Force 11 data citation principles (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind: anonymise text and files, cover sheet separate, replace self-references with "author", do not list own works under "Author" in the references (instructions copy). Preprints are allowed and do not prevent submission; authors of accepted papers must update the status of any preprint with the published DOI (same copy, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **AI use** | Unverified for the journal (see AI Policy); a new permanent AI section exists (home page copy 2026-11-17) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; OA charge chosen after acceptance, amount not readable (see Open Access) |
| **Funding and permissions** | Authors must name their funding sources, or state there are none, during submission; authors are asked to obtain permission from rights holders before submitting extracts, figures or tables from other works; accepted authors sign a copyright assignment form and confirm the article is original (instructions copy 2024-04-06, https://web.archive.org/web/20240406044740id_/https://academic.oup.com/applij/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Prior and parallel publication** | The editors assume the article is unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere in the submitted form or a modified version (instructions copy) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 2. Per layer: Crossref counts (methods, topics by wording, authors) 3 (abstract coverage 72.2%; no country data); journal-specific policies and guidelines 2 (all publisher pages read only as Wayback copies; the instructions copy is from 2024-04-06 and no AI section was in it); editorial board 3 (exact counts from a 2026-04-19 copy); experiential layer 1 (SciRev n = 5; LetPub shows 1 review whose text was not in the fetched page).

**Sources cited across this entry:**
- Wayback copies of academic.oup.com pages: journal home (2026-11-17), About (2026-04-18), Editorial_Board (2026-04-19), General_Instructions (2024-04-06), why-publish (2024-11-19), OUP author-use-of-AI page (2026-04-29), OUP charges-licences-and-self-archiving (2026-05-18) and accepted-manuscript embargo list (2026-04-03); all fetched with curl through the Wayback `id_` route, each URL given where used
- https://api.crossref.org/journals/0142-6001 and https://api.crossref.org/journals/1477-450X ; Crossref works for the window (471 records, 340 with abstract)
- https://api.openalex.org (scaffold values only; the OpenAlex daily budget returned HTTP 429 when the paged pull was attempted, so no further OpenAlex request was made)
- https://scirev.org/journal/applied-linguistics/ and https://scirev.org/reviews/applied-linguistics/ ; https://www.letpub.com/journal-selector/journal/11682 ; https://journalreviews.princeton.edu/2022/09/17/applied-linguistics (secondary, 2022)

**Method notes:** Crossref abstracts were stripped of JATS markup and counted locally with the regexes below (Python re, IGNORECASE except A24). 471 records, 340 with abstract; share = hits / 340. Regex hits count records, not occurrences. Broad patterns over-count: A11 matches "L2" and "language learners", A13 matches "teacher" and "instruction", A15 matches the word "AI" in any case, A23 matches "power" and "critical".

**Keyword regexes (exact):**
- A1 `\b(regression|mixed[- ]effects?|ANOVA|statistical(ly)?|quantitative|questionnaires?|surveys?|Likert|structural equation|factor analysis)\b`
- A2 `\b(experiment(s|al)?|quasi-experimental|randomi[sz]ed|intervention|pre-?test|post-?test|control group)\b` ; A3 `\bcorp(us|ora)\b`
- A4 `\b(interviews?|focus groups?|thematic analysis|narrative inquiry|grounded theory|qualitative)\b` ; A5 `\bethnograph\w*\b`
- A6 `\b(conversation analysis|discourse analysis|multimodal\w*|critical discourse)\b` ; A7 `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b`
- A8 `\b(meta-analys[ei]s|systematic review|research synthesis|scoping review)\b` ; A9 `\bautoethnograph\w*\b`
- A10 `\b(theoretical(ly)?|conceptual(ly)?|theori[sz](e|es|ed|ing))\b` ; A11 `\b(second language|L2|SLA|foreign language|EFL|ESL|language learners?)\b`
- A12 `\b(translanguag\w*|multilingual\w*|bilingual\w*|plurilingual\w*)\b` ; A13 `\b(classrooms?|teachers?|pedagog\w*|instruction(al)?)\b` ; A14 `\b(assessment|language testing|proficiency tests?)\b` (31, 9.1%)
- A15 `\b(artificial intelligence|generative AI|ChatGPT|large language models?|LLMs?|AI)\b` ; A16 `\b(indigenous|endangered|revitali[sz]ation|minoriti[sz]ed|decoloni\w*)\b`
- A17 `\b(raci(al|alized|st|sm)|racio\w*|whiteness|antiracis\w*)\b` ; A18 `\b(gender(ed)?|queer|LGBT\w*|transgender|non-?binary|sexuality|feminis\w*)\b`
- A19 `\b(migrants?|refugees?|immigrants?|asylum)\b` ; A20 `\b(language polic(y|ies)|language planning|linguistic landscape)\b`
- A21 `\b(workplace|healthcare|forensic|legal|medical|clinical|courts?)\b` ; A22 `\b(implications?)\b` ; A23 `\b(critical|ideolog\w*|inequalit\w*|social justice|power)\b`
- A24 (case-sensitive) `\b(I|[Ww]e|[Oo]ur|[Mm]y)\b`

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Applied relevance**: the journal's instructions list no clear real-world connection, minimal application, implications only at the end, and no empirical basis as signs a paper does not fit (Framing Requirements; instructions copy 2024-04-06).
- **Length**: accepted manuscripts should not exceed 8,500 words including all print material except the abstract; the abstract should not exceed 175 words (Format).
- **Anonymisation**: submissions must be anonymised, with names on a cover sheet and self-references replaced by "author" (Peer Review).
- **Prior and parallel publication**: the editors assume the work is unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere (Practical Concerns).
- The instructions are a 2024 copy; the live rules, including any AI-use rule, were not read.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher prints medians of 25 and 27.5 days for first and final decision in 2025, while SciRev entries (n = 5) report first rounds of 11.7 to 26 weeks and a desk rejection after 117 days (Review Cycle Time). The two are not reconciled.
- **Cost**: hybrid journal; the OA charge was not readable and is chosen after acceptance (Open Access). Funder-mandated immediate open access would require the OA route (instructions copy).
- **Self-archiving**: on the non-OA route the accepted manuscript can be placed in a repository after a 12-month embargo (Preprint Policy).
- **Anonymisation work**: self-citations must be neutralised and the references purged of own works under "Author" (Peer Review).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical studies of language in education, the workplace, healthcare, legal and media settings with explicit practical implications: second or foreign language wording appears in 137 of 340 abstract-records, classroom wording in 136, "implications" in 70 (Orientation, Framing Requirements).
- Qualitative, quantitative, corpus and discourse-analytic designs alike: each of A1, A3, A4 and A6 exceeds 12% of abstract-records (Methodological Preferences).
- Work on translanguaging, AI and language, and social-justice themes, which the journal features in a virtual issue and a new section (Sensitive Topics).

### Not Recommended For

- Purely theoretical or methodological contributions without applied discussion: the instructions list these among poor fits (Framing Requirements).
- Authors who need verified current AI-use rules, an APC amount or an acceptance rate before choosing: none could be read (AI Policy, Open Access, Metrics).
- Formal-linguistic analysis without an applied setting; this follows from the framing rule above, not from a count (Framing Requirements).

### Rejection Fallback Chain
